items.title: Competing-risk data, cause-specific hazard measures, and cumulative incidence
items.statement: For finitely many latent event times with a unique first cause, define the observed first time and cause, its right-censored record, all-cause survival, cause-specific event subdistributions and hazard measures, and cause-specific cumulative-incidence functions.

items.title: Cause-specific cumulative incidence as an integral against its hazard measure
items.statement:
For every cause $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$ and every $t\ge0$, the cumulative
incidence decomposes as
$$F_k(t)=\int_{[0,t]}S(u-)\,d\Lambda_k(u).$$
If $\nu_k$ has a Lebesgue density $f_k$ and $S(u)>0$ for every $u\in(0,t]$,
then $d\Lambda_k(u)=\lambda_k(u)\,du$ for Lebesgue-a.e. $u\in(0,t]$ with
$\lambda_k(u):=f_k(u)/S(u)$, and
$$F_k(t)=\int_0^tS(u)\lambda_k(u)\,du.$$
items.strategy: Construct the cause-specific hazard as the measure with density 1/S(u−) relative to the cause-event subdistribution, verify that zero-risk times carry no event mass, and apply the density-integration identity.

items.title: Aalen–Johansen cumulative-incidence estimator
items.statement: For a fixed horizon and finite right-censored competing-risk sample, compute the all-cause product-limit survival and each cause-specific cumulative incidence by processing tied event times together and multiplying each cause increment by pre-event survival.

items.title: Fixed-time Aalen–Johansen outputs are well-defined statistics
items.statement:
Fix $n\ge1$, finite $K$, and $t\ge0$, and let
$$\mathcal X=\big([0,\infty)\times\{0,1,\ldots,K\}\big)^n$$
carry its Borel sigma-algebra as a Euclidean subspace, where status $0$ denotes
censoring and status $k$ denotes an observed cause-$k$ event. Let $\mathsf E$
be any statistical experiment with sample space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal B(\mathcal X))$.
Equip
$\mathbb R^{K+1}$ with its Borel sigma-algebra. The output vector of
[[alg-aalen-johansen-cumulative-incidence-estimator]] at horizon $t$ is a
measurable map $\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^{K+1}$ and hence a statistic in
$\mathsf E$. Every event-time denominator $Y(u)$ is positive.
items.strategy: Express risk and cause counts using finitely many Borel comparisons, use the event-at-time risk convention to bound each event count by its risk count, and compose the resulting measurable finite sums, products, and positive-denominator ratios.

title: Competing risks and cumulative incidence — Examples

items.title: The observed first time and cause do not identify the latent joint failure-time law
items.statement: The law of the observed first time and cause uniquely determines the joint law of the latent cause-specific failure times without additional assumptions.
items.strategy: Construct two distinct finite latent-time laws with no ties and compute their identical pushforward laws under the first-time/cause observation map.

items.title: Higher competing mortality lowers incidence in a two-time table
items.statement: Two exact 16-subject competing-risk tables have the same cause-1 event fractions at each observed event time but different cause-2 mortality; the Aalen–Johansen cause-1 incidence is lower in the high-competing-mortality table, while the cause-specific Kaplan–Meier complement is 7/16 in both.
items.strategy: Compute all-cause risk sets and Aalen–Johansen increments at times 1 and 2, then recode cause-2 failures as censorings and calculate the two cause-specific product limits.
